Search and Learning Have Limits

engineering note (test fixture), 2026

Search and learning are the two general methods that turn more
computation into more capability, and the well-known lesson is
that over a long enough horizon they beat hand-built domain
knowledge. But "scales with computation" is not the same as
"always wins", and it is worth being precise about when these two
methods actually pay off. This note adds a condition to that known
fact rather than proposing a competing method of its own.

The first precondition is that computation actually keeps growing
for the problem at hand. Search and learning are ways to convert a
computation budget into capability; if that budget is fixed and
small, a carefully hand-built method can stay ahead, simply because
there is no extra computation for the general method to ride on.

The second precondition is a structure the method can exploit.
Search needs a space it can enumerate or sample together with a
signal that separates good states from bad ones. Learning needs a
training signal that is plentiful and cheap to evaluate. On a task
that exposes neither a searchable structure nor a learnable signal,
pouring more computation into search or learning buys very little.

So the two general methods are not a free lunch. They dominate in
the long run only where computation keeps growing and the task
exposes a structure to search or a signal to learn from. Stated as
a boundary on the general-method fact: search and learning scale
only when both conditions hold, so a knowledge entry about them
should carry those conditions, not merely the headline that they
scale.

This note makes no new headline claim of its own. It only records
the conditions under which the two already-known general methods,
search and learning, actually convert computation into capability.
